b: I previously posted about the risky state of Medicare Advantage plans. Here is the latest.

Kaiser Family Foundation’s October analysis found that 4.3 million Medicare beneficiaries will lose their current private plans at year’s end. 3.1million in Medicare Advantage plans with drug coverage and 1.2 million in standalone Part D plans.
That can mean losing doctors and specialists, paying more out of pocket or giving up extra benefits. Even those whose plans aren’t discontinued shouldn’t assume their coverage will stay the same.
